name: Green Goddess Gazpacho
description: Whipped crema, lemon oil, quick pickles
tableside: A cold soup for the season — bright, herbaceous, and refreshing. The whipped crema adds richness and the quick pickles cut through it. A great lighter starter for a guest who wants something elegant before a heavier main.

dairy.note: Whipped crema contains dairy. Can be omitted on request.

eggs.note: Crema may contain eggs — check with kitchen.

vegan.note: Can be made vegan by omitting the crema.

key_terms.definition: A cold Spanish soup traditionally made from raw blended vegetables. Originally from Andalusia, it is served chilled and is inherently refreshing — particularly effective as a palate opener before a rich meal.

A classic American dressing style from the 1920s, traditionally made with tarragon, chives, parsley, anchovies, and mayonnaise. The modern interpretation here focuses on the herbal, green character without the anchovy base.
Vegetables briefly cured in vinegar and salt rather than fermented — bright, acidic, and crunchy. They provide acidity and texture contrast to the smooth, rich gazpacho base.

chef_notes: A cold soup in a warm restaurant — make sure the guest knows it's served chilled. Some guests are surprised.

name: Cream of Carrot Soup
description: Chipotle cream, ginger spiced croutons, arugula
tableside: A classic cream soup elevated by heat and spice — chipotle adds smokiness and warmth, ginger croutons add crunch and aromatics, arugula on top adds bitterness to balance. Warming and satisfying without being heavy.

dairy.note: Contains cream. Cannot be made dairy-free.

gluten.note: Croutons contain gluten. Can be omitted for a GF version.

key_terms.definition: A smoked, dried jalapeño pepper. Chipotle peppers have a deep, smoky heat that is less sharp than fresh jalapeño — they add warmth and complexity without overwhelming spice.
House-made croutons seasoned with ginger — they add textural contrast to the smooth soup and an aromatic warmth that complements both the carrot's sweetness and the chipotle's smokiness.

chef_notes: Croutons can be removed for gluten-free guests. The soup itself is GF without them.

name: Gem Lettuce
description: Herbed goat cheese, red onion, candied pecans, Rubyfrost apples, creamy balsamic
tableside: A composed salad built around contrasts — the creamy goat cheese against the crisp lettuce, the sweet candied pecans against the tart balsamic, the Rubyfrost apple adding a juicy brightness. Elegant and approachable.

dairy.note: Contains goat cheese. Can be removed to make dairy-free.

nuts.note: Contains candied pecans. Can be removed to make nut-free.

vegan.note: Can be made vegan by removing goat cheese. Confirm balsamic dressing with kitchen.

key_terms.definition: A cross between butter lettuce and romaine — smaller and more compact than romaine, with the crispness of romaine and the sweetness of butter lettuce. Sturdy enough to hold a creamy dressing without wilting.
A proprietary apple variety developed in New York, known for its sweet-tart balance and exceptional crunch. Stays crisp longer than most apples and has a distinctive red-pink flesh.
A balsamic vinaigrette emulsified with a creamy element — richer and more coating than a standard vinaigrette, with the sweet-acid character of aged balsamic vinegar.

sourcing.name: Rubyfrost Apple
sourcing.description: A trademarked apple variety developed through Cornell University's apple breeding program in New York. Known for its extraordinary crispness and balanced sweet-tart flavor, it holds up well in composed salads without browning quickly.

chef_notes: Both the goat cheese and candied pecans can be removed independently — a guest can have one without the other. The salad works well without either.

name: Arugula Salad
description: Shaved asparagus, radish, pecans, puffed quinoa, honey mustard vinaigrette
tableside: A textural salad — peppery arugula, crunchy puffed quinoa, shaved asparagus for freshness, radish for bite, pecans for richness. The honey mustard ties it together with sweetness and acid. Light but satisfying.

dairy.note: No dairy.

nuts.note: Contains pecans. Can be removed to make nut-free.

eggs.note: Honey mustard vinaigrette may contain eggs — check with kitchen.

vegan.note: Confirm honey mustard dressing is vegan with kitchen — honey makes this not strictly vegan.

key_terms.definition: A peppery salad green native to the Mediterranean. Its bitter, spicy character pairs naturally with sweet and acidic dressings — honey mustard vinaigrette is a classic complement.

Quinoa that has been heated until the grains expand and become light and crispy — similar in texture to puffed rice. Adds crunch and a nutty flavor while being naturally gluten-free and high in protein.
Asparagus ribboned thin with a peeler and served raw — a fresher, more delicate preparation than cooked asparagus that adds crunch and grassy flavor without losing the asparagus character.

chef_notes: Pecans can be removed. The salad is naturally gluten-free and dairy-free without modification.

name: Spinach Salad
description: Roasted badger flame beets, goat cheese, fried shallots, lemon vinaigrette
tableside: Built around the Badger Flame beet — a yellow and red striped variety with a sweeter, milder flavor than standard beets. Goat cheese for creaminess, fried shallots for crunch and savory depth, lemon vinaigrette to brighten everything.

dairy.note: Contains goat cheese. Can be removed to make dairy-free.

gluten.note: Fried shallots may be dusted in flour — check with kitchen for GF guests.

vegan.note: Can be made vegan by removing goat cheese. Confirm shallot preparation with kitchen.

key_terms.definition: A specialty beet variety developed at the University of Wisconsin, known for its striking yellow and red striped flesh and sweeter, more delicate flavor than standard red beets. Worth mentioning to guests who think they don't like beets.
Thinly sliced shallots fried until crispy — they add a savory, caramelized crunch that is different from raw onion. A classic garnish in Southeast Asian and French cooking.

sourcing.name: Badger Flame Beet
sourcing.description: A specialty variety developed through the University of Wisconsin's plant breeding program. Sweeter and milder than standard red beets, with striking striped flesh — worth describing to guests who might otherwise pass on a beet salad.

chef_notes: Worth mentioning the Badger Flame beet by name — guests who claim not to like beets are often surprised by how mild this variety is.

name: Carrot Humus
description: Wild boar ragù, marinated feta, toasted pita
tableside: Not your standard hummus — carrot as the base instead of chickpea, topped with a wild boar ragù that adds richness and game character, and marinated feta for salt and creaminess. An unexpected combination that works beautifully as a shared starter.

dairy.note: Contains feta cheese. Can be omitted on request.

gluten.note: Toasted pita contains gluten. Can be substituted with GF cornbread at Chef's discretion.

key_terms.definition: A Middle Eastern dip or spread traditionally made from cooked chickpeas blended with tahini, lemon, and garlic. This version uses carrot as the base instead of chickpea, producing a sweeter, more delicate result.

A slow-cooked Italian-style meat sauce made from wild boar — a leaner, more intensely flavored meat than domestic pork. The ragù is braised low and slow to break down the tough game meat into a rich, savory topping.
Feta cheese cured in olive oil with herbs and aromatics — softer and more complex than plain feta, with additional herbal flavor from the marinade.

chef_notes: When guests hear 'hummus' they expect chickpea — worth mentioning the carrot base to set expectations. The wild boar ragù is the star of the dish.

name: Loaded Pierogies
description: Cheddar, bacon crumble, dill crema, crispy shallots
tableside: Comfort food elevated — pierogies loaded with cheddar, topped with bacon crumble, crispy shallots, and dill crema. Rich, satisfying, and crowd-pleasing. The table that orders these never regrets it.

dairy.note: Contains cheddar and crema. Cannot be made dairy-free.

gluten.note: Pierogi dough contains gluten. Cannot be made GF.

key_terms.definition: Boiled or fried dumplings originating from Eastern Europe — most commonly Polish — traditionally filled with potato, cheese, or meat. The dough is soft and slightly chewy, similar to fresh pasta.
A soured cream sauce infused with fresh dill — the herb's bright, slightly anise-like flavor cuts through the richness of the cheese and bacon filling.

chef_notes: One of the most reliably loved dishes on the menu — good recommendation for tables that can't decide on a starter.

name: Poached White Asparagus
description: Mousseline, marinated salmon roe, bourbon truffle salt
tableside: White asparagus is a European delicacy — more delicate and subtly sweet than green asparagus, with none of the bitterness. The mousseline is a luxurious butter sauce, the salmon roe adds brininess and pop, and the bourbon truffle salt ties it together. One of the most elegant starters on the menu.

shellfish.note: Salmon roe is fish roe, not shellfish. Safe for shellfish allergies.

dairy.note: Mousseline contains butter and egg yolks. Cannot be made dairy-free.

eggs.note: Mousseline sauce is made with egg yolks.

vegan.note: Contains fish roe, butter, and eggs.

key_terms.definition: Asparagus grown underground or covered to block sunlight, which prevents chlorophyll development and keeps the stalks white. More tender and subtly flavored than green asparagus, with a slightly sweeter, nuttier character. A springtime delicacy in European cuisine, particularly in Germany and France.

A hollandaise sauce lightened with whipped cream — the addition of cream makes it airier and more delicate than standard hollandaise, while retaining the rich butter and egg yolk base. A classic French sauce for asparagus.
The eggs of salmon, cured in salt — large, bright orange pearls that burst with briny, oceanic flavor. Distinct from sturgeon caviar but similarly luxurious in texture and presentation.
A finishing salt infused with truffle and bourbon — the truffle adds earthy depth, the bourbon adds subtle sweetness and complexity. A house-made condiment that ties the dish together.

chef_notes: Worth explaining what white asparagus is to guests who haven't encountered it — the unfamiliarity can cause hesitation. Once they understand it's more delicate than green asparagus, most are interested. This is also a strong wine pairing opportunity — a bottle conversation dish.

name: Baked Brie
description: Cherry jam, candied pecans
tableside: Simple and reliable — baked brie with cherry jam and candied pecans. Rich, melty, sweet, and crowd-pleasing. Great for a table that wants a shareable starter without too much adventure. The candied pecans can be removed for nut allergies.

dairy.note: It is brie — dairy is the dish.

nuts.note: Contains candied pecans. Can be removed to make nut-free.

gluten.note: No gluten in the dish itself — if served with bread or crackers, those would contain gluten.

key_terms.definition: A soft-ripened French cheese made from cow's milk, known for its creamy interior and edible white rind. When baked, the interior melts to a liquid consistency while the rind holds its shape — creating a vessel of warm, runny cheese.

chef_notes: Pecans can be removed easily. One of the most approachable starters on the menu — reliable recommendation for tables that are indecisive.

name: BBQ Bone Marrow
description: Apricot jam, mint gremolata, ciabatta
tableside: Bone marrow is beef butter — rich, silky, and completely unlike anything else on the menu. The apricot jam cuts through the fat with sweetness and acid, the mint gremolata keeps it bright and fresh. Spread it on the ciabatta like the world's most indulgent toast. For guests who haven't had it, lead with the texture description.

dairy.note: Bone marrow is beef fat, not dairy.

gluten.note: Ciabatta contains gluten. Can be omitted — ask kitchen to substitute GF cornbread.

key_terms.definition: The soft, fatty tissue inside beef leg bones. When roasted, it becomes liquid and silky — essentially concentrated beef fat with a rich, deeply savory flavor. Guests who haven't had it often compare it to the most intensely flavored butter they've ever tasted.

An Italian condiment made from parsley, garlic, and lemon zest. Traditionally served with ossobuco, it provides bright, herbal acidity to cut through rich braised or roasted dishes. Here it serves the same purpose — lifting the heaviness of the marrow.
An Italian flatbread with an open, airy crumb and chewy texture. The crust is sturdy enough to hold the marrow without disintegrating, and the mild flavor doesn't compete with the dish.

chef_notes: Guests who haven't had bone marrow are often hesitant — the concept sounds unusual. Lead with 'beef butter' and the spreading motion on the ciabatta. Once they visualize it, most are in. One of the best dishes for adventurous tables. Strong bottle pairing opportunity.

name: Salmon Belly
description: Bourbon cured and baked, apple vinegar, radish, arugula, mustard seed gastrique
tableside: The fattiest, richest cut of the salmon — cured in bourbon, which adds sweetness and depth before baking. The apple vinegar and mustard seed gastrique provide the acidity and sharpness that fatty fish needs. A sophisticated starter that shows restraint and technique.

shellfish.note: No shellfish — salmon is a fish, not a shellfish.

dairy.note: No dairy.

gluten.note: Bourbon cure may contain gluten — check with kitchen for GF guests.

key_terms.definition: The ventral cut of the salmon — the fattiest part of the fish, with a higher fat content than the fillet. The fat distributes through the flesh as it cooks, keeping it moist and adding rich flavor.
A curing mixture incorporating bourbon — the whiskey's sweetness and vanilla character infuse into the salmon during the curing process, adding complexity beyond a standard salt-sugar cure.
A French sauce made by reducing sugar and vinegar together to create a sweet-sour syrup. Here the mustard seeds add texture and sharp heat to the sweet-acid gastrique base.
Whole mustard seeds have a milder, nuttier flavor than ground mustard — when used in a gastrique they pop with a gentle heat and provide textural contrast.

chef_notes: The bourbon cure is a house preparation — worth mentioning to guests who are interested in the detail. Good conversation piece and a natural bridge to the bar program.

name: Shrimp and Grits
description: Whiskey cream, spinach, caramelized onion, aleppo chili crisp
tableside: A Southern classic elevated — the whiskey cream adds depth and sweetness to the sauce, aleppo chili crisp brings warm heat and a fruity, slightly smoky spice. Hearty enough to be a light main for some guests. One of the most satisfying starters on the menu.

shellfish.note: Contains shrimp — a shellfish. Cannot be modified.

dairy.note: Grits and cream sauce contain dairy. Cannot be made dairy-free.

gluten.note: Whiskey cream sauce may contain gluten — confirm with kitchen.

key_terms.definition: Ground corn cooked into a porridge — a staple of Southern American cuisine. Stone-ground grits have more corn flavor and texture than quick-cook versions. They become creamy and rich when cooked with butter and dairy.

A condiment made from Aleppo pepper — a Syrian chili known for its moderate heat, fruity flavor, and slightly oily texture. Milder and more complex than standard chili flakes, with notes of cumin and dried fruit.
A cream sauce built on a whiskey reduction — the alcohol burns off during cooking, leaving behind the grain sweetness and vanilla character of the whiskey as a flavor base for the cream.

chef_notes: Clarify for shellfish allergy guests immediately — there is no modification possible. Worth flagging at the order stage.

name: Parker House Rolls
description: With ramp butter
tableside: House-baked Parker House rolls with ramp butter — soft, pillowy, and rich. Ramps are a wild spring onion with a garlicky, chive-like flavor. If the table is ordering bread, these are the move.

dairy.note: Contains butter. Cannot be made dairy-free.

gluten.note: Bread contains gluten. Cannot be made GF — see GF Cornbread.

eggs.note: Parker House rolls typically contain eggs.

key_terms.definition: A classic American dinner roll originating from the Parker House hotel in Boston in the 1870s — soft, slightly sweet, and folded before baking to create the distinctive pull-apart shape. Rich with butter and milk.

A wild spring onion (Allium tricoccum) native to eastern North America — one of the first plants to emerge after winter. They taste like a cross between garlic and green onion, with a more complex, slightly pungent character. Highly seasonal and foraged rather than farmed.

chef_notes: Ramps are highly seasonal — they appear in spring and their availability window is short. When they're on the menu, worth mentioning their seasonal nature to guests who appreciate local and foraged ingredients.

name: GF Skillet Cornbread
description: With pear butter
tableside: House-baked gluten-free cornbread in a skillet, served with pear butter. A genuine GF option that stands on its own — not a compromise. The pear butter adds a delicate sweetness that complements the savory corn.

dairy.note: Contains butter. Cannot be made dairy-free.

key_terms.definition: A fruit butter made by cooking pears down to a thick, spreadable consistency — similar to apple butter. Sweeter and more delicate than apple butter, with a floral quality that pairs well with savory cornbread.

chef_notes: The go-to recommendation for GF guests who want bread service. Also works as a substitute bread for GF guests ordering the bone marrow or carrot hummus.

name: Butcher Salad
description: Crème fraîche vinaigrette, tomato, cucumber, lardons, spit roasted meat
tableside: The butcher salad is topped with meat carved directly from whatever is on the rotisserie that night — it changes with the daily feature. A lighter way to experience the rotisserie program, or a great addition for a table that ordered a main and wants the rotisserie experience too.
ingredients: Spit roasted meat from the rotisserie

dairy.note: Crème fraîche vinaigrette contains dairy. Can be subbed for another dressing at Chef's discretion.

key_terms.definition: French for 'fresh cream' — a cultured cream with a nutty, tangy, slightly sour flavor. Thicker and richer than sour cream, with a higher fat content that prevents it from curdling when heated.
Small cubes of fatty bacon — a French culinary term. They add savory richness, smokiness, and textural contrast to salads and cooked dishes. Typically rendered until crispy before use.

chef_notes: The meat on this salad reflects whatever is on the rotisserie that night — know the daily feature and communicate it when describing this dish. It changes Tuesday through Saturday.

name: Joyce Farm Chicken
description: Truffle orzo mac and cheese, glazed carrots, garlic honey jus — half $29 / whole $58
tableside: Joyce Farm chicken from North Carolina — heritage breed, pasture raised, antibiotic free. Cooked on the rotisserie, which bastes the bird continuously in its own fat and produces the most evenly cooked, juicy result possible. The truffle orzo mac and cheese is the kind of side dish that tables fight over. Available as half or whole.

dairy.note: Truffle mac and cheese contains dairy. Cannot be made dairy-free without modifying the side.

gluten.note: Orzo is wheat pasta — contains gluten.

key_terms.definition: A cooking method where meat is mounted on a rotating spit over or in front of heat. The constant rotation bastes the meat in its own juices and fat, producing extraordinarily even cooking and a deep, caramelized exterior.

Chicken breeds that predate industrial farming — slower-growing, with more time to develop flavor and more complex muscle structure than commercial breeds. Joyce Farm's birds are raised to near maturity before processing, producing meat with significantly more flavor.
A rice-shaped pasta — small enough to be used like rice but with the texture and chew of pasta. Used here in a truffle mac and cheese preparation.
A pan sauce made from the roasting juices of the chicken, enriched with garlic and honey — sweet, savory, and deeply aromatic.

sourcing.name: Joyce Farms
sourcing.description: A family-owned farm and agricultural operation in North Carolina, specializing in heritage breed poultry and meat. Their chickens are pasture raised with open outdoor access after six weeks of age, antibiotic-free, and grown to full natural maturity before processing. The result is chicken with significantly more flavor and better texture than commercially raised birds. Used by acclaimed restaurants throughout the Mid-Atlantic and Southeast.

chef_notes: The half chicken is the right call for most guests — the whole bird is for a table that really wants to commit. Clarify which they want at the order stage. The truffle mac and cheese is genuinely exceptional — worth mentioning specifically.

name: Whole Roasted Fish
description: Carrot, ginger, red pepper, peanut & coconut curry, peanut, smoked cashews
tableside: A whole fish on the rotisserie — the preparation is dramatic and the result is extraordinary. The coconut curry broth is bold and aromatic, the smoked cashews add crunch and depth. This is for a table that wants a centerpiece dish and isn't afraid of commitment. Worth confirming the guest is comfortable with a whole fish presentation.

dairy.note: No dairy. Coconut milk is not dairy.

nuts.note: Contains peanuts and cashews. Cannot be made nut-free.

soy.note: Curry preparation may contain soy — confirm with kitchen.

key_terms.definition: A sauce built on a base of coconut milk and curry spices — aromatic, slightly sweet, with warmth from the spice blend. Southeast Asian in inspiration, it pairs naturally with fish and delivers bold flavor without the heaviness of a cream-based sauce.
Cashews that have been cold or hot smoked to add a woody, aromatic depth to their natural buttery flavor. They add both texture and complexity to the dish.

chef_notes: Confirm the guest is comfortable with a whole fish presentation — some guests are surprised or uncomfortable with the head and tail. Also confirm nut allergies before ordering — the peanuts and cashews cannot be removed.

name: Ibérico Rack of Pork
description: With aleppo chili crisp · served with duck fat potatoes · limited availability
tableside: Ibérico pork is not regular pork — it comes from the Black Iberian pig of Spain and Portugal, whose diet of acorns gives the fat an extraordinary nutty, complex flavor. The rack is spit roasted whole and carved tableside. The duck fat potatoes are as good as they sound. Limited availability — when it's gone, it's gone.

dairy.note: No dairy.

key_terms.definition: Refers to the Black Iberian pig, native to the Iberian Peninsula. Ibérico pork is renowned for its intramuscular fat — the pigs' diet of acorns (bellota) during the finishing period infuses the fat with oleic acid and complex aromatic compounds that produce a flavor unlike any other pork. The fat of Ibérico pork is nutritionally similar to olive oil.

The Spanish word for acorn — the defining element of premium Ibérico production. Pigs with access to acorn pasture (dehesa) during the montanera season develop the distinctive fat composition that makes Ibérico pork extraordinary.

Potatoes roasted in rendered duck fat — the fat produces extraordinary crispness on the exterior while keeping the interior fluffy. Duck fat has a higher smoke point than butter and a rich, savory flavor that makes the best roast potatoes in the world.

sourcing.name: Ibérico Pork
sourcing.description: The Black Iberian pig is found in the dehesa — the oak woodland pastures of southwestern Spain and Portugal. Pigs classified as 'bellota' (acorn-fed) spend their final months grazing freely on acorns, producing a fat with exceptional nutritional and flavor qualities. Ibérico products are among the most prized and expensive in the world — Jamón Ibérico de Bellota commands prices rivaling fine wine. Serving it as a spit-roasted rack is an unusually dramatic preparation of an already exceptional ingredient.

chef_notes: Limited availability — know when it's running low and communicate to the table proactively. The Ibérico story is worth telling — guests who know it will be thrilled, and those who don't will be fascinated. One of the best bottle pairing opportunities of the week.

name: Rack of Lamb
description: With basil & pine nut-arugula pesto · served with duck fat potatoes · limited availability
tableside: A full rack of lamb from the rotisserie — the most elegant of the weekly features. The basil and pine nut pesto cuts through the richness of the lamb with brightness and herbal freshness. Duck fat potatoes alongside. Wednesday night's centerpiece.

dairy.note: Pesto may contain Parmesan — confirm with kitchen.

nuts.note: Pesto contains pine nuts. Cannot be made nut-free without removing the pesto.

key_terms.definition: A premium cut consisting of the rib section of the lamb — the individual chops still attached to the rack bone. It presents dramatically at the table and is considered one of the finest cuts of lamb available.

A classic Ligurian sauce traditionally made from basil, pine nuts, garlic, Parmesan, and olive oil. This version adds arugula, which contributes a peppery bitterness that complements the richness of the lamb.
The edible seeds of pine trees — small, elongated, and buttery. They are technically a tree nut and a common allergen. The pine nut in pesto provides richness and a subtle sweetness.

chef_notes: Confirm pine nut allergy before ordering — the pesto cannot be fully removed as it is integral to the dish's composition. Strong wine pairing opportunity — this is the week's most classic red wine dish.

name: Tomahawk Ribeye
description: With salsa verde · served with duck fat potatoes · limited availability
tableside: The tomahawk is the most dramatic plate in the restaurant — a full ribeye with the long bone left intact, carved tableside from the rotisserie. The salsa verde provides herbal brightness and acid against the richness of the beef. Thursday nights are built around this dish.

dairy.note: No dairy.

key_terms.definition: A bone-in ribeye steak with an extended rib bone left intact — typically 6 to 8 inches of bone, resembling a tomahawk axe handle. The bone adds flavor during cooking and creates an extraordinary tableside presentation. One of the most prized beef cuts for both flavor and spectacle.

A green herb sauce — the Italian version typically uses parsley, capers, anchovies, garlic, and olive oil. The acid and brightness of the sauce is specifically designed to cut through the richness of fatty meats like beef. Unlike Mexican salsa verde, the Italian version is not cooked or tomato-based.

Cooking a ribeye on the rotisserie is unusual — most high-end steaks are grilled or pan-seared. The rotating spit allows the fat to continuously baste the exterior as it renders, producing a crust and internal juiciness that is difficult to achieve by other methods.

chef_notes: The most dramatic dish of the week — know how to describe the presentation to tables before they order. This should be mentioned proactively to any table that looks like they want something special on a Thursday. The highest bottle pairing potential of any dish on the menu.

name: Prime Rib
description: With horseradish cream · served with duck fat potatoes · limited availability
tableside: The weekend anchor — prime rib from the rotisserie, carved to order, served with horseradish cream and duck fat potatoes. Classic, satisfying, and exactly what a Friday or Saturday night guest is looking for. Know when it's running low.

dairy.note: Horseradish cream contains dairy. Can be served without the cream on request.

key_terms.definition: A standing rib roast — a large, bone-in cut of beef from the primal rib section, slow roasted to develop a deep crust while maintaining a juicy, pink interior. 'Prime' refers to the cut's position on the animal (the prime rib primal) rather than USDA quality grade, though the best prime rib is indeed USDA Prime.

A condiment made from grated horseradish root folded into cream — pungent, sharp, and bright, it provides the acid and heat contrast that fatty roast beef needs. Traditional accompaniment to prime rib and roast beef in British and American cuisine.

chef_notes: Weekend staple — Friday and Saturday guests often come specifically for this. Know when it's available and when it's running low. Horseradish cream can be omitted for dairy-free guests.

name: Pan Seared Salmon
description: Cauliflower purée, braised cauliflower, pickled cauliflower
tableside: Three preparations of cauliflower — purée, braised, and pickled — each adding a different texture and dimension. The purée is rich and creamy, the braised adds depth, the pickled adds brightness and acid. The salmon is pan seared for a crispy skin. Chef's preference is medium rare — confirm with the guest.

shellfish.note: Salmon is a fish, not a shellfish.

dairy.note: Cauliflower purée contains butter and/or cream. Ask kitchen for dairy-free modification.

key_terms.definition: Cooking protein in a very hot pan to develop a browned, caramelized crust through the Maillard reaction — the same chemical process that browns bread and caramelizes onions. For salmon, pan searing creates a crispy skin while leaving the center moist.

The same vegetable prepared in three distinct ways — purée for richness and creaminess, braised for depth and softness, pickled for acidity and crunch. This technique showcases the range of one ingredient while creating textural and flavor contrast on the plate.

chef_notes: Chef's preference is medium rare — confirm temperature with the guest before ordering. Can be cooked to any temperature requested. The cauliflower purée can be modified for dairy-free guests.

name: Pan Seared U12 Scallops
description: Blood orange risotto, savoy spinach, sesame
tableside: U12 means under 12 per pound — these are large, premium scallops. Pan seared hard for a caramelized crust, served over blood orange risotto that's bright and slightly sweet. The sesame adds an unexpected nuttiness. One of the most elegant mains on the menu.

shellfish.note: Scallops are shellfish. Cannot be modified.

dairy.note: Risotto contains butter and Parmesan. Cannot be made dairy-free without changing the dish significantly.

nuts.note: No nuts — sesame is a seed, not a tree nut, but it is its own allergen.

key_terms.definition: A size designation — 'U12' means under 12 scallops per pound. Larger scallops sear more effectively because they have more surface area to crust before the center overcooks. U12 are considered large premium scallops in the market.

A citrus variety with dark red flesh caused by anthocyanin pigments — the same compounds that color red wine. Blood oranges are more complex than standard oranges, with berry and raspberry notes alongside the citrus character.

Note: sesame is classified as a major food allergen by the FDA (as of 2023) — it is distinct from tree nuts and peanuts. Guests with sesame allergies should be made aware that this dish contains sesame seeds.

chef_notes: Flag shellfish allergy immediately — no modification possible. Also flag sesame as a separate allergen — it became a federally recognized major allergen in 2023 and some guests may not think to mention it.

name: Belgian Seafood Stew
description: PEI mussels, shrimp, market fish, potatoes, leeks
tableside: A coastal Belgian-style stew — PEI mussels, shrimp, and whatever the market fish is tonight, in a broth built from the shellfish themselves. Potatoes and leeks make it hearty. This is a rustic, satisfying dish that rewards guests who want something warming and complete.

shellfish.note: Contains mussels and shrimp. Cannot be modified for shellfish allergies.

dairy.note: Broth preparation may include butter — confirm with kitchen.

key_terms.definition: Mussels from Prince Edward Island, Canada — one of the world's most prized mussel-growing regions. PEI mussels are farm-raised on ropes suspended in the clean, cold Atlantic waters, producing sweet, plump mussels with virtually no grit.
A mild, sweet member of the allium family — related to onion and garlic but with a more delicate flavor. They break down during cooking to add body and sweetness to broth-based dishes.
The fish component of this dish changes based on market availability — ask the kitchen what it is each evening. It could be any firm white fish suitable for stewing.

sourcing.name: PEI Mussels
sourcing.description: Prince Edward Island, Canada produces some of the finest mussels in the world. The cold, clean Atlantic waters and rope-farming method produce mussels that are consistently sweet, plump, and clean — without the grit common in wild-harvested mussels.

chef_notes: Ask the kitchen what the market fish is each evening — guests may ask. Flag shellfish allergy immediately, no modification possible.

name: Pan Seared Rockfish
description: Butter braised turnips, pee wee potatoes, dill crema
tableside: Rockfish — also called striped bass — is a Mid-Atlantic fish with firm, white flesh and a clean, mild flavor. Butter braised turnips add earthiness and richness, pee wee potatoes for heartiness, dill crema for brightness. A well-balanced, complete plate.

shellfish.note: Rockfish is a fin fish, not a shellfish.

dairy.note: Butter and dill crema contain dairy. Can be modified — check with kitchen.

key_terms.definition: A saltwater fish native to the Atlantic Coast of North America — the official state fish of Maryland, Virginia, and several other East Coast states. Known for its firm white flesh and clean, mild flavor that pairs well with butter-based preparations.

Extra-small potatoes, typically under 1 inch in diameter — they cook quickly and have a thin skin that crisps beautifully when roasted. Their small size means they can be served whole, which is visually appealing.

Cooking vegetables in butter with a small amount of liquid over gentle heat — the butter coats and enriches the vegetable while the slow cooking develops sweetness and depth. Turnips braised this way become tender and sweet, losing their raw sharpness.

chef_notes: Rockfish is a local Mid-Atlantic fish — worth mentioning the regional connection to guests who appreciate local sourcing.

name: Braised Demkota Short Rib
description: Garlic mashed cauliflower, blistered broccolini, truffle madeira jus
tableside: Demkota short rib — a premium South Dakota producer known for exceptional quality beef. Braised low and slow until the collagen breaks down and the meat becomes fork-tender, served with truffle Madeira jus that's deeply savory and aromatic. One of the most satisfying dishes on the menu.

dairy.note: Garlic mashed cauliflower contains butter. Can be modified — check with kitchen.

gluten.note: Madeira jus may be thickened with flour — confirm with kitchen for GF guests.

key_terms.definition: A combination cooking method — first searing the meat at high heat to develop a crust, then cooking it low and slow in liquid. The collagen in tough cuts like short rib breaks down over time into gelatin, thickening the cooking liquid into a rich sauce and making the meat extraordinarily tender.

A cut from the beef chuck or plate — richly marbled with fat and connective tissue. These qualities make it ideal for braising, which transforms the tough collagen into silky gelatin. Short rib is one of the most flavorful beef cuts when properly prepared.

A fortified wine from the Portuguese island of Madeira — known for its extraordinary longevity and complex, oxidative character. Used in sauces, it adds depth, dried fruit notes, and acidity that enhances beef-based jus significantly.

A prized underground fungus with an intensely earthy, musky aroma — one of the most valuable ingredients in European fine dining. Used in small quantities as a finishing element, it adds depth and luxury to the Madeira jus.

sourcing.name: Demkota Ranch Beef
sourcing.description: Demkota Ranch in South Dakota produces premium beef from cattle raised on high-quality feed and handled with careful animal husbandry practices. Their beef is known for consistent marbling and superior flavor — a step above commodity beef in quality and traceability.

chef_notes: The braising process takes hours — this dish cannot be rushed or modified significantly. The truffle Madeira jus is a signature element. Strong bottle pairing opportunity — this is the red wine dish on the land section.

name: Wienerschnitzel from Pork
description: Dill potato salad, lingonberry jam
tableside: Traditional Austrian schnitzel made with pork rather than the classic veal — thinner, lighter, and more accessible. Breaded and pan-fried until golden, served with a dill potato salad and lingonberry jam. The lingonberry jam is the key — its tartness cuts through the richness of the fried pork perfectly.

shellfish.note: The fryer may cook shellfish products — confirm with kitchen to prevent cross-contamination for severe allergies.

dairy.note: No dairy in the dish itself.

nuts.note: The fryer may cook nut-containing products — confirm with kitchen.

gluten.note: Breadcrumb crust contains gluten. Cannot be made GF.

eggs.note: Schnitzel breading typically uses egg wash.

key_terms.definition: A traditional Austrian dish of thin, breaded, pan-fried cutlets. Wiener Schnitzel is technically required to use veal by Austrian law, but 'Schnitzel vom Schwein' (pork schnitzel) is the most common everyday version. The name means 'Viennese cutlet.'

A small, tart red berry native to Scandinavian and northern European forests — similar in flavor to cranberry but smaller and more intensely sour. Lingonberry jam is a traditional Scandinavian accompaniment to fried and game meats, where its tartness cuts richness effectively.

A European-style potato salad dressed with vinegar and dill rather than mayonnaise — lighter and more acidic than American-style potato salad. The dill provides herbal freshness that complements both the potato and the schnitzel.

chef_notes: The fryer cross-contamination note for shellfish and nut allergies is important — always check with the kitchen before confirming this dish for guests with severe allergies. Traditionally made with veal — mentioning that this version uses pork helps set expectations.

name: Green Hill Pork Loin
description: Smoked puttanesca, kalamata olives, barley risotto, basil
tableside: A leaner cut than the short rib — pork loin with a smoked puttanesca that brings intensity and brininess from the olives and capers. The barley risotto is a heartier, nuttier alternative to standard risotto. Sophisticated and satisfying for guests who want pork without the richness of the daily features.

shellfish.note: Traditional puttanesca contains anchovies — confirm whether this version does.

dairy.note: Barley risotto may contain Parmesan — confirm with kitchen.

gluten.note: Barley contains gluten. Cannot be made GF without changing the risotto.

key_terms.definition: An Italian sauce originating in Naples, traditionally made with tomatoes, olives, capers, anchovies, garlic, and chili. Bold, briny, and intensely savory — the name translates roughly to 'in the style of a lady of the night,' though the true etymology is disputed. Here it is smoked, adding another layer of depth.

Risotto made with pearl barley instead of Arborio rice — the barley has more fiber and a nuttier, earthier flavor than standard risotto rice. It takes longer to cook and retains more texture, giving the dish a heartier character.

A Greek olive variety from the Kalamata region of the Peloponnese — large, dark purple-black, and intensely flavored with a meaty texture and rich, briny taste. Significantly more complex than standard black olives.

chef_notes: Confirm whether the puttanesca contains anchovies — relevant for vegetarian guests and shellfish allergy guests. Barley contains gluten — cannot be made GF without removing the risotto entirely.

name: Spring Chicken Cavatelli
description: Asparagus, English peas, radish, cured egg yolk
tableside: A spring pasta — cavatelli with fresh asparagus, English peas, and radish, finished with a cured egg yolk that adds richness and a silky, almost carbonara-like quality when broken into the pasta. Lighter than a cream pasta but deeply satisfying.

dairy.note: May contain Parmesan or butter — confirm with kitchen.

gluten.note: Cavatelli is wheat pasta. Cannot be made GF.

eggs.note: Contains cured egg yolk — a featured element, not removable.

key_terms.definition: A small Italian pasta shaped like a tiny hot dog bun — the rolled shape captures sauce inside the curl. Originally from southern Italy, particularly Puglia and Campania, where it is typically made with semolina and water rather than egg.

An egg yolk cured in a salt and sugar mixture until it firms up to a texture similar to hard cheese — it can then be grated or sliced over dishes. The curing concentrates the yolk's rich, savory flavor and creates a luxurious, umami-rich garnish.
Standard garden peas — specified as 'English' to distinguish them from sugar snap peas or snow peas. Sweet, fresh, and tender when in season.

chef_notes: The cured egg yolk is a signature element — worth describing to guests who aren't familiar with the technique. It cannot be removed as it is integral to the dish.

name: Basil Pesto Risotto
description: Pecorino, tomato confit, asparagus, garlic chips
tableside: The vegetarian main — and it stands entirely on its own. Basil pesto risotto with pecorino, slow-cooked tomato confit, asparagus, and crispy garlic chips. Rich, aromatic, and deeply satisfying. One of the best vegetarian dishes on any menu in the area.

dairy.note: Contains Pecorino Romano cheese. Cannot be made dairy-free without losing the core character of the dish.

nuts.note: Basil pesto traditionally contains pine nuts — confirm with kitchen.

gluten.note: Rice is gluten-free. Confirm no wheat-based thickeners are used with kitchen.

key_terms.definition: An Italian rice dish cooked by gradually adding warm stock to short-grain rice (typically Arborio or Carnaroli) while stirring continuously. The starch released from the rice creates a creamy consistency without added cream.
Tomatoes slow-cooked in olive oil at low temperature for an extended period — they become intensely concentrated, sweet, and jammy, losing their raw acidity and developing deep umami flavor.

A hard Italian cheese made from sheep's milk — sharper, saltier, and more pungent than Parmesan, which is made from cow's milk. The sheep's milk gives it a distinctive tangy quality that pairs particularly well with basil and vegetable-based dishes.
Thinly sliced garlic cloves fried until golden and crispy — they add a savory, caramelized crunch and intense garlic flavor as a garnish.

chef_notes: The best vegetarian main on the menu — worth mentioning proactively to vegetarian guests rather than waiting for them to find it. Confirm pine nut presence in the pesto for nut allergy guests.

name: Rotisserie Carrots
description: Tahini crema, pine nuts, aleppo chili crisp
tableside: Carrots cooked on the rotisserie — the fat from the meats above bastes them as they roast, giving them a depth of flavor impossible to achieve in a conventional oven. Tahini crema for richness, pine nuts for crunch, aleppo chili crisp for warmth.

dairy.note: Tahini crema may contain dairy — confirm with kitchen.

nuts.note: Pine nuts are tree nuts — allergen concern. Can be removed.

vegan.note: Confirm tahini crema preparation — may contain dairy.

key_terms.definition: A paste made from ground sesame seeds — nutty, slightly bitter, and rich. Used extensively in Middle Eastern and Mediterranean cooking. When emulsified with lemon and water it becomes a creamy sauce.

A condiment made from Aleppo pepper — a Syrian chili with moderate heat, fruity flavor, and slight oiliness. Milder and more complex than standard chili flakes, with notes of cumin and dried fruit. The 'crisp' refers to the texture of the oil-fried pepper flakes.

chef_notes: Pine nuts can be removed for nut allergies. Worth mentioning the rotisserie preparation — the carrot has absorbed the drippings from the meats above, which makes it unusually flavorful.

name: Crispy Brussels Sprouts
description: Smoked blue cheese, fried shallots, honey mustard vinaigrette
tableside: Brussels sprouts that will convert any non-believer — fried until genuinely crispy, tossed in honey mustard, topped with smoked blue cheese and fried shallots. The smoked blue cheese is the move. Rich, savory, and slightly sweet. One of the most reliable sides on the menu.

shellfish.note: The fryer may cook shellfish — confirm with kitchen for severe allergies.

dairy.note: Smoked blue cheese contains dairy. Can be omitted on request.

nuts.note: The fryer may cook nut-containing products — confirm with kitchen.

gluten.note: The fryer may be used for breaded items containing gluten — confirm with kitchen.

eggs.note: Honey mustard vinaigrette may contain eggs — confirm with kitchen.

key_terms.definition: Blue cheese that has been cold-smoked — the smoke adds a woody, aromatic depth to the already pungent, funky character of the blue cheese. The combination of smoke and blue cheese funk is particularly effective against sweet or acidic accompaniments like honey mustard.

chef_notes: Multiple fryer cross-contamination concerns — always check with kitchen for severe allergy guests. Blue cheese can be removed for dairy-free. One of the most popular sides — good to mention proactively.

name: Buttermilk Spätzle
description: Cheese, caramelized onion
tableside: German egg noodle dumplings made with buttermilk — chewy, rich, and deeply comforting. Tossed with cheese and caramelized onion. Think of it as the Austrian mac and cheese. Perfect alongside the Wienerschnitzel or the short rib.

dairy.note: Contains buttermilk and cheese. Cannot be made dairy-free.

gluten.note: Spätzle is a wheat-based pasta. Cannot be made GF.

key_terms.definition: A German egg noodle or dumpling — made by pressing a soft dough through a colander or spätzle press directly into boiling water. The irregular shape and chewy texture are characteristic. The name means 'little sparrows' in Swabian German dialect.

The acidic liquid left after churning butter from cream. In baking and cooking, its acidity tenderizes dough and adds a subtle tang. In spätzle, buttermilk produces a more tender dumpling than water alone.

Onions cooked slowly over low heat for 30–45 minutes until their natural sugars develop into deep sweetness — a completely different flavor from sautéed or raw onion. They add sweetness, depth, and umami to the rich cheese and pasta base.

chef_notes: A natural pairing suggestion alongside the Wienerschnitzel — both are Austrian in spirit. Also excellent with the short rib.

name: Brookie Sundae
description: Chocolate raspberry ice cream, espresso meringue, hot fudge, whipped cream
tableside: A brookie is a brownie-cookie hybrid — the base combines both textures. Topped with chocolate raspberry ice cream, espresso meringue, hot fudge, and whipped cream. The espresso meringue is the standout element — airy and slightly bitter against the sweetness of everything else.

dairy.note: Contains ice cream, whipped cream, and hot fudge. Cannot be made dairy-free.

gluten.note: Brookie base contains gluten. Cannot be made GF.

eggs.note: Meringue is made from egg whites. Brookie likely contains eggs.

key_terms.definition: A hybrid baked good combining brownie and cookie in one — typically layered or swirled so both textures are present in each bite. The combination of fudgy brownie and chewy cookie produces a more complex texture than either alone.
Meringue — whipped egg whites and sugar — flavored with espresso. Light and airy with a slightly bitter coffee character that cuts through the sweetness of the sundae components.

chef_notes: The espresso meringue is the detail worth mentioning — guests who don't notice it listed will be pleasantly surprised. Good pairing with Hennessy VS or the Nonino amaro.

name: Berry Heart
description: Strawberry & white chocolate mousse, vanilla sponge cake, raspberry gel, blueberry-lavender sorbet
tableside: The lightest and most delicate dessert on the menu — strawberry and white chocolate mousse, vanilla sponge cake, raspberry gel, and blueberry-lavender sorbet. Beautiful presentation. For guests who want something sweet but not heavy to end the meal.

dairy.note: Contains white chocolate and mousse components. Cannot be made dairy-free.

eggs.note: Mousse and sponge cake contain eggs.

key_terms.definition: A light, airy preparation made by folding whipped cream or egg whites into a flavored base — the incorporated air creates the characteristic light, cloud-like texture.
A concentrated raspberry purée set with a gelling agent (typically agar or gelatin) — more intense and clean in flavor than a sauce, with a firm, glossy texture.
A dairy-free frozen dessert made from fruit purée and sugar — blueberry and lavender is a classic Provençal pairing, where the floral herb complements the berry's sweetness.

chef_notes: The lightest dessert — ideal for guests who say they 'don't want anything too heavy.' The presentation is particularly beautiful. Good pairing with the Di Majo Norante Moscato.

name: S'mores Chocolate Torte
description: Toasted meringue, smoked chocolate cremeux, devil's food, peanut butter, smoked salt
tableside: A composed dessert built around the s'mores concept — toasted meringue, smoked chocolate cremeux, devil's food cake, peanut butter, and smoked salt. Every component is elevated and each one earns its place. The smoked salt is the key — it makes the chocolate more intense and the sweetness more balanced.

dairy.note: Contains chocolate and cremeux. Cannot be made dairy-free.

nuts.note: Contains peanut butter. Peanuts are technically legumes but are a major allergen. Cannot be made nut-free.

soy.note: Chocolate may contain soy lecithin — confirm with kitchen for soy allergies.

key_terms.definition: A French pastry term for a smooth, dense, creamy preparation made from cream, egg yolks, and chocolate or other flavoring — richer than mousse and less set than ganache. The texture is like the inside of a very good truffle.
Chocolate that has been cold-smoked to add a subtle woody, smoky character. The smoke enhances the chocolate's bitter notes and adds complexity without being obvious.
An intensely chocolatey American cake — darker, moister, and more deeply flavored than standard chocolate cake, typically made with hot water or coffee to bloom the cocoa and develop flavor.

chef_notes: Peanut allergy is non-negotiable — cannot be modified. Confirm before ordering. Good pairing with Ardbeg Uigeadail — the peated Scotch against smoked chocolate is a remarkable combination for adventurous guests.

name: Black Forest Strudel
description: Mascarpone, port cherry reduction, Callebaut chocolate, chantilly, Luxardo cherries
tableside: A refined take on Black Forest cake in strudel form — mascarpone filling, port cherry reduction, Callebaut chocolate, chantilly cream, and Luxardo cherries. The Callebaut chocolate is Belgian and considered one of the world's finest. The Luxardo cherries are the real thing — not the neon red kind. Elegant and satisfying.

dairy.note: Contains mascarpone and chantilly cream. Cannot be made dairy-free.

eggs.note: Strudel pastry and chantilly likely contain eggs.

soy.note: Callebaut chocolate may contain soy lecithin — confirm for soy allergies.

key_terms.definition: An Italian fresh cream cheese from Lombardy — extraordinarily rich and creamy, with a mild, slightly sweet flavor. The base of tiramisu and a luxurious filling for pastries.

A Belgian chocolate producer considered one of the finest in the world — used by professional pastry chefs globally. Callebaut chocolate has a higher cocoa content and more complex flavor than mass-market chocolate, with fruity and roasted notes.

Premium maraschino cherries from the Luxardo distillery in Italy — made from Marasca cherries preserved in their own syrup. Intensely flavored, dark, and not artificially colored or flavored. Completely different from American-style maraschino cherries.
The French term for lightly sweetened, vanilla-flavored whipped cream — named after the Château de Chantilly near Paris.

sourcing.name: Callebaut Chocolate
sourcing.description: Barry Callebaut is a Belgian chocolate manufacturer founded in 1850, producing chocolate from bean to couverture. Their chocolate is used by professional pastry chefs and chocolatiers worldwide for its consistent quality and complex flavor profile.

sourcing.name: Luxardo Cherries
sourcing.description: Produced by the Luxardo distillery in Torreglia, Italy — the same company that makes the famous Maraschino liqueur. Their preserved Marasca cherries are hand-harvested and preserved in the distillery's own syrup, producing cherries with genuine cherry flavor rather than the artificial sweetness of American maraschino cherries.

chef_notes: Worth mentioning both Callebaut and Luxardo by name to guests who appreciate quality ingredients. Good pairing with Graham's 20 Year Tawny or the Doisey-Védrines Sauternes.

name: Cheese Board
description: Chef's selection of three cheeses, seasonal jam, crostini
tableside: Three cheeses selected by Pastry Chef Amanda Siever — the selection changes based on what's best at the moment. Always a range of textures and intensities. Ask the kitchen for tonight's selections before describing it to the table. Best with the Sauternes or a tawny port.

dairy.note: It is a cheese board.

nuts.note: Some cheese pairings may include nuts — confirm tonight's accompaniments with kitchen.

gluten.note: Crostini contains gluten. Can be omitted or substituted with GF crackers if available.

key_terms.definition: Small slices of toasted or grilled bread — lighter and crispier than bruschetta. Used as a vehicle for cheese and accompaniments.

chef_notes: Always check with the kitchen for tonight's cheese selection before describing this dish — it changes regularly. The Cheese Board with the Doisey-Védrines Sauternes is one of the great classic pairings on the menu. Mention it.

name: Sorbet Trio
description: Pineapple-watermelon, mango & passion fruit, strawberry-apricot
tableside: Three sorbets — pineapple-watermelon, mango and passion fruit, and strawberry-apricot. Light, refreshing, and dairy-free. The right call for guests who want something sweet to close the meal without heaviness. Also the default dessert recommendation for vegan and dairy-free guests.

dairy.note: Sorbet is dairy-free — made from fruit purée and sugar, not cream.

vegan.note: Vegan — confirm no honey or other animal products with kitchen.

key_terms.definition: A frozen dessert made from fruit purée and sugar syrup — no dairy, no eggs. Lighter and more intensely fruit-flavored than ice cream or gelato. The absence of fat means the fruit flavor is direct and clean.

chef_notes: The only fully vegan and dairy-free dessert option on the menu — know this and offer it proactively to guests with dietary restrictions. The Di Majo Norante Moscato pairs beautifully with the tropical sorbets.
